$comment: Ledger of /kaizen findings a human has explicitly reviewed and declined to act on. Read and written by the kaizen skill — see .claude/skills/kaizen/SKILL.md, 'Step 2 — filter against declined findings' and 'Step 6 — decline / un-decline a finding' for the full read/write/undo contract. Entries are appended ONLY when a user explicitly declines a finding during a live /kaizen run — never seeded speculatively, never written by kaizen on its own initiative. TO UN-DECLINE: delete the matching object from the 'declined' array below (by hand, or by asking /kaizen to do it — see SKILL.md) and commit the change; the finding is reconsidered with fresh evidence on the next /kaizen run. A declined finding also drops off this ledger's effect automatically, with no edit needed, the moment its id no longer matches anything /kaizen computes (e.g. a gate's yield crosses back out of the verdict band that was declined) — see the 'id' field note below.

schema.id: string, required. '<category>:<subject>:<claim>'. category is one of the /kaizen signal steps (mr-cycle-time, ci-duration, gate-skip, prepush-runtime, mandate-reality, doc-drift, gate-yield). subject names the concrete thing the finding is about (a gate name, a CI job name, a CLAUDE.md rule/section, a file path) using the same slug /kaizen would print for it. claim names the specific shape of the finding (e.g. fast-path-candidate, slow-outlier, frequently-skipped, stale-rule, mismatch). The id is deliberately NOT a line number, a report timestamp, or free text copied from the finding's prose — none of those survive a re-run. Composing subject+claim means a decline survives as long as /kaizen keeps making the same claim about the same subject, and stops matching (so the finding silently reappears, un-suppressed) the moment the claim changes shape — e.g. a gate declined as 'fast-path-candidate' that later becomes 'load-bearing' is a different id and is never suppressed by the old entry.
schema.declined_on: string, required. ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the session in which the human declined the finding.
schema.reason: string, required. The human's own stated reason, in their words or a faithful paraphrase — not the assistant's guess at one. This is what makes a decline a recorded decision instead of a silent omission.
schema.subject: string, optional. One-line human-readable restatement of what was declined, for a reader skimming the raw JSON without cross-referencing a /kaizen report. Not used for matching.
